correctness.rationale: Soulimani--Gulbrandsen's full primary description gives the intersection \(D\) of the two \(\operatorname{Hilb}^{2t+2}(\mathbb P^3)\) components as incident line pairs or planar double lines carrying the spatial embedded point. The incident-line stratum has dimension 3+4=7, while the double-line stratum has dimension at most 6, so \(\dim D=7\). Almeida--Jardim--Oliveira give the irreducible 11-fold pair component \(\mathcal P_2\), its proper dominant map to the 8-fold skew-line Hilbert component, and the two pair-space images in the sheaf moduli space. Thus \(Z=\mathcal P_1\cap\mathcal P_2\) is a proper closed subset of \(\mathcal P_2\), so \(\dim Z\le10\), while every fiber has dimension at least three and the 7-dimensional boundary forces \(\dim Z\ge10\). Irreducibility of each forgetful-map fiber \(\mathbb P H^0(E(1))\) proves \(\Psi(Z)=\overline{\mathcal R}\cap T\). On a general incident-line boundary point the associated scheme is nonplanar, and AJO Proposition 3.9 gives \(h^0(E(1))=1\), so no dimension is lost. The bundled verifier correctly checks the arithmetic dimensions but is not used in place of these geometric inputs.
correctness.risk: The argument is set-theoretic at the final component intersection and does not determine scheme structure or irreducibility.

final_claim: For the two irreducible components \(\overline{\mathcal R}\) and \(T(-1,2,4,1)\) of the Gieseker moduli space \(\mathcal M(-1,2,2)\) on \(\mathbb P^3\), one has \(\dim(\overline{\mathcal R}\cap T)=10\); hence the intersection is a divisor in the 11-dimensional reflexive component and has codimension five in the 15-dimensional elementary-transformation component.
limitations: Set-theoretic dimension only; no irreducibility or scheme-structure claim.
